cards.text: After this, Jesus goes out and sees a tax collector named Levi, sitting at the tax booth. Now, most folks speed UP when they pass a tax booth. Not Jesus.

cards.question: Jesus sees Levi sitting at his tax booth and speaks to him. What does Jesus tell Levi?
Jesus tells Levi, “Follow Me.” True or false: Levi asks for time to close up his tax booth first.

cards.text: Levi gets up, leaves everything and follows Him, and then he hosts a great banquet for Jesus at his house. The man LEFT EVERYTHING, and I can't walk away from a tray of warm cookies without looking back three times!

cards.question: Levi hosts a great banquet for Jesus at his house. Who makes up the large crowd there?
True or false: everyone eating at Levi's banquet is a tax collector.

cards.text: Not everybody's celebrating, because every party has somebody standing by the door with their arms crossed. Here it's the Pharisees, a group of religious leaders, and their scribes, and they bring a complaint to Jesus' disciples.

cards.question: The Pharisees and their scribes complain to Jesus' disciples. What are they complaining about?

answers.text: Eating with tax collectors and sinners

cards.text: Jesus answers, and of ALL things, He starts talking about doctors.

cards.question: Jesus answers the complaint about who He eats with. Who does He say needs a doctor?
Jesus says He has not come to call the righteous, but ___, to repentance.
Next, the Pharisees and their scribes bring up fasting and praying. True or false: they say Jesus' disciples fast and pray more than anyone.

cards.text: They say the disciples of John the Baptist and the Pharisees often fast and pray, but Jesus' disciples keep on eating and drinking. In other words: “Your guys NEVER leave the table!”
Jesus answers with a picture from a wedding, with the bridegroom right there with His guests. And nobody shows up to a wedding to sit in the corner looking gloomy.

cards.question: Jesus asks if you can make the guests of the bridegroom ___ while He is with them.
True or false: Jesus says a time will come when the bridegroom will be taken from His guests.

cards.text: And when the bridegroom is taken from them, Jesus says, then they will fast.
Jesus tells them a parable, and it starts with clothes. No one tears a piece of cloth from a new garment and sews it on an old one.

cards.question: Say someone tears a patch from a new garment and sews it onto an old one. What does Jesus say happens?

answers.text: He tears the new garment too
The old garment looks brand new
The patch shrinks and falls off

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the patch from the new garment will match the old one.

cards.text: Then a second picture: no one pours new wine into old wineskins.

cards.question: Say someone pours new wine into old wineskins anyway. What does Jesus say happens?

answers.text: The skins burst and the wine spills
The skins stretch and hold it

cards.text: Burst skins, spilled wine, and the wineskins are ruined. It's like cramming a fresh batch into a cookie box held together with tape, and you KNOW how that ends.

cards.question: So instead, Jesus says, new wine is poured into ___ wineskins.
One last line: Jesus says no one who has been drinking old wine wants new. What does that person say?

findings.problem: The joke blends the comparison with the Bible setting. 'Speed UP when they pass' is a modern driving image, but it is attached to the Bible's tax booth. The result is neither a clean toll-booth picture nor a clean first-century picture, so it doesn't click right away.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.

findings.problem: 'In other words:' marks the quoted line as a paraphrase of what the speakers said in Luke 5:33, yet it is in quotation marks. It also overstates their claim, turning 'keep on eating and drinking' into 'NEVER leave the table.' The line is presented as their meaning, not as Papa Dorin's own made-up joke line.

rule.text: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included. A paraphrase uses no quotation marks. His own made-up lines in jokes can use quotation marks.

findings.problem: This story card is a bare restatement of Luke 5:35 with none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: 'Then a second picture: no one pours new wine into old wineskins.' is stripped down, with no Papa Dorin voice. Card 1 of this stop is nearly as flat. Most of the parable stop reads as plain narration.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Stop 2 opens with the same card-type sequence as Stop 1: story, multiple choice, true/false, story, multiple choice. Stop 1 itself also starts with a repeating story, multiple choice, true/false pattern.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The question already says the person 'doesn't want new.' That setup rules out the wrong answers 'The new is better' and 'They taste the same,' so the right answer is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
